requirements.title: External procedures are defined externally or by non-Fortran means
requirements.definition: An external procedure is defined by an external subprogram or by a means other than Fortran.

pending.external-subprogram-defines-external-pro: Compile a main program calling external function ext_answer() defined in a separate external function returning 42; initialize result variable to -777 and expect 42. Wrong-resolution companion also imports a module function ext_answer returning -999; using the module name instead changes the result to -999, while the external declaration companion preserves 42.
pending.non-fortran-means-defines-external-proce: Source-use entry only: records a procedure defined by means other than Fortran through a BIND(C) interface; executable evidence belongs to the Clause 18 interoperability owner rules, not this external-procedure definition.

requirements.title: Internal procedures are internal subprogram procedures with host association and local names
requirements.definition: An internal procedure is defined by an internal subprogram; its name is not a global identifier and it has access to host entities by host association.

pending.internal-subprogram-defines-internal-pro: Place internal subroutine set_answer inside a main program; initialize actual to -1, call set_answer, and expect 42.
pending.internal-procedure-name-not-global: Create two separate host procedures, each with an internal function named local_answer; the default host-local companion returns 41 from the first host and 42 from the second, while a wrong global-resolution sentinel external local_answer returns -999 and would make either host result -999.
pending.internal-procedure-host-association: In a host procedure initialize host integer base to 40; internal function add_two reads base and returns base+2, producing 42. Wrong-resolution sentinel companion provides an external add_two returning -999; resolving away from the internal host-associated procedure changes the result to -999.

requirements.title: Internal subprograms may appear in main, external, or module subprogram hosts
requirements.definition: Internal subprograms are permitted in a main program, an external subprogram, or a module subprogram.

pending.internal-subprogram-in-main-program: Use a main program CONTAINS internal function answer() returning 42 and assign its result to a variable initialized to -4; expect 42.
pending.internal-subprogram-in-external-subprogr: Use an external subroutine wrapper containing internal function answer() returning 42; main calls wrapper and expects an INTENT(OUT) actual to become 42.
pending.internal-subprogram-in-module-subprogram: Use a module subroutine wrapper containing internal function answer() returning 42; main USEs the module, calls wrapper, and expects 42.

requirements.definition: An internal subprogram is not permitted to appear within another internal subprogram.

requirements.title: Module procedures are defined by module subprograms or supplied by intrinsic modules
requirements.definition: A module procedure is defined by a module subprogram, or is a specific procedure supplied by an intrinsic module.

pending.module-subprogram-defines-module-procedu: Define module m containing function answer() returning 42; USE m in a program, call answer(), and expect 42. Wrong-resolution sentinel companion defines an external answer returning -999; omitting USE m selects the external and makes the mismatch observable.
pending.intrinsic-module-specific-procedure-is-m: Source-use inventory records one specific procedure from ISO_FORTRAN_ENV or an IEEE intrinsic module as a module procedure. A future default companion USEs the intrinsic module specific and observes its required value; wrong-resolution sentinel supplies an external of the same local name returning -999 so accidental non-module resolution is observable.

requirements.title: Subprograms define procedures for FUNCTION, SUBROUTINE, and ENTRY statements
requirements.definition: A subprogram defines a procedure for its SUBROUTINE or FUNCTION statement and also one procedure for each ENTRY statement it contains.

pending.subprogram-defines-procedure-for-functio: Compile external subroutine primary(x) that assigns 42; main initializes actual to -6, calls primary, and expects 42.
pending.entry-statement-defines-additional-proce: After ENTRY execution rules are registered, compile an external subroutine with ENTRY alternate(x) assigning 42; call alternate from main with actual initialized to -6 and expect 42.
